newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil expert says will talk to NYMEX, others.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil expert says will talk to NYMEX, others.

text.p: An expert reviewing the International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) gas oil contract said on Thursday she would talk to U.S. market traders, among other industry players, to help formulate possible reforms of Europe's main winter energy market.

British energy consultant Sally Clubley added in a telephone interview that the aim of the inquiry was to suggest possible improvements to the contract, target of recent criticsm following a duel between two trading houses, to ensure that it continued to meet the needs of the industry.
She suggested she would look in particular at enforcement.

"I was just talking to one broker who said that at the end if everyone hates me I'll have done my job," Clubley said in a wry acknowledgment of sharp differences in views of the contract's management.
The IPE announced earlier it had appointed Clubley to carry out an independent review of its gas oil contract following what it called recent "strains", in particular difficulties with delivery.
An IPE statement said it expected the review to be completed by mid-March and anticipated Clubley would look at the way similar contracts were handled in the United States.
"I'll certainly talk to NYMEX (the New York Mercantile Exchange), and to traders who trade both NYMEX and the IPE, as well as those who just trade one (market)," Clubley told Reuters.

She added: "It's a long time since the gas oil contract was last looked at closely overall, and I think they feel it is time, because of the things they are picking up from the industry, to see whether the contract is meeting the needs of the industry ... It's not an admission of failure (by the IPE)."

"There is a feeling that it may not be so much the rules (that are at issue) so much as the enforcement of the rules. People do feel the exchanges do operate very differently. In a time of very regulated markets there may be grounds for looking at this."
The IPE added that in the event that Clubley recommended any changes, it expected to introduce such changes before the end of 1997.

The IPE statement made no mention of a showdown over the delivery of the November gas oil contract between AIC and Cargill that triggered widespread criticism by European oil traders of the conduct of the continent's main winter oil market.

Traders said the duel paralysed much of the Rotterdam barge trade market, curbing liquidity, distorting supply patterns and blunting the IPE's price discovery function. Some have called for tighter contract terms. Others have called for tougher fines, expressing admiration for NYMEX's practice of big spot fines for misbehaviour.
Clubley said in response to a question that she would not be probing the AIC-Cargill standoff.
"This (inquiry) is the future, not the past. The IPE has all the procedures in place (to handle the AIC-Cargill affair)," she said.
Clubley has 16 years' experience in the oil industry and lectures at theCollege of Petroleum and Energy Studies at Oxford.

She formely managed E D and F Man's London trading desk and has also been a member of the IPE board. She holds an honours degree in biochemical engineering and previously worked as a business journliast.
